description: PAINT-FROM-SAMPLE — appearance as an order-k code sampled from a contour-bounded region, painted over the whole region as a cheap pass, and the residual taken where the paint was wrong. The order k FALLS OUT of the residual (PROTOCOL §13): paint flat, and escalate only where the paint is refuted at the field's own alphabet resolution. Boundaries are strict local maxima of |Δ| — an exact comparison with NO threshold and NO scale. Luminance is STRUCTURE (it defines the regions); appearance is a SIGN (it is sampled and painted). v1.1.0 adds the EDGE-ANCHORED DECAYING GRADIENT behind a second flag: the order-2 excursion is anchored at the boundary that sourced it and decays over the region's OWN mean geodesic depth, so the code is the fitted plane AT the edge and the order-1 constant FAR from it — never an extrapolation across the far field. Ships INERT (paint=0, pdecay=0) so every committed result reproduces (PROTOCOL §9).

microtheory.name: paint_from_sample
microtheory.description: A surface's appearance is not computed per cell. It is SAMPLED as an order-k code over a region and PAINTED; the residual is where the paint was wrong, and it is the residual — not a parameter — that decides the order.

rules.name: pt_delta
rules.comment: Per cell: the forward |Δplum| to the east (pd_e) and south (pd_s) neighbour, and whether that link exists at all (pd_has_e / pd_has_s). Luminance is STRUCTURE — it is what defines the regions; appearance is a SIGN and is only ever sampled and painted. A link to an ABSENT or UNSENSED neighbour contributes nothing (Sum over the empty set = 0), which is why the blind spot never invents an edge. Reads ONLY raw plum/prow/pcol/psensed on self and neighbours — NO cross-node computed dependency, so firing order is irrelevant. Fires once (pdelta_done).

rules.name: pt_block
rules.comment: THE BOUNDARY, and it carries NO threshold and NO scale (PROTOCOL §13): the link east of c is BLOCKED iff its |Δ| is STRICTLY GREATER than the |Δ| of the link on either side of it along the same axis — non-maximum suppression written as an exact comparison. A uniform field (all Δ equal 0) and a LINEAR RAMP (all Δ equal) therefore have NO boundary anywhere and stay ONE region; a step has one; a Craik-O'Brien cusp has one AT THE CUSP and none at its shoulders, so each flat region KEEPS its ramp. A missing flank contributes 0 (Sum over the empty set). Fires once all neighbours' deltas are in (the handshake — never an ordering assumption).

rules.name: pt_seed
rules.comment: pregion := pidx. Every cell starts as its own region; the flood then merges. Fires once (pseed_done).

rules.name: pt_flood
rules.comment: THE REGION: pregion := min(self, every neighbour reachable across an UNBLOCKED link), to the run_rules fixpoint. Monotone non-increasing and bounded below by the region's minimum pidx, so it terminates. The HUB FALLS OUT — the unique cell with pidx == pregion — so no region node is minted and no id is assigned by the adapter. An UNSENSED cell (the optic disc) has no blocked links, so it joins the surround's region and is painted from it.

rules.name: pt_hub
rules.comment: MARK the region's representative. The hub already FALLS OUT of the flood (pidx == pregion); this rule only writes that fact onto the graph as `phub`, so the ADAPTER never has to compute it. Without this the read-back would need an `if` comparing two graph attributes in Python — a query, but one the graph can just as easily answer itself (CLAUDE.md).

rules.name: pt_fit1
rules.comment: THE SAMPLE, order 1: on the region's hub, the region mean of plum and papp plus the centroid — pooled over the field-anchored set of cells sharing this hub's pregion, counting ONLY cells that carry an observation (psensed). ONE sampling rule, applied to every stimulus identically; there is no per-stimulus branch anywhere in this seed. NOT done-flagged: the flood may still be merging, so the fit is idempotent and re-settles with it (it is a pure function of its inputs, so it cannot dither).

rules.name: pt_fit2
rules.comment: THE SAMPLE, order 2: a separable least-squares plane about the region centroid — one slope per coordinate per channel. Declared as a SEPARABLE estimate, not an optimal joint fit: for a region whose row and column coordinates are correlated it is the marginal slope. `Div` returns 0.0 on a zero denominator, which is exactly right here — a single-row region HAS no row slope — and is the reason no epsilon appears. Reads pmean_*/pcen_* written by pt_fit1 on the SAME node; pt_fit1 does not read anything pt_fit2 writes, so the pair has no cycle and the fixpoint settles it.

rules.name: pt_anchor
rules.comment: THE ANCHOR. panchor := 1 iff this cell touches a BLOCKED link — its own east/south link, or the east link of its west neighbour, or the south link of its north neighbour. A blocked link IS a strict-|Δ| maximum, i.e. a luminance edge, so 'edge-anchored' here means anchored at a luminance discontinuity and NOTHING ELSE. In particular THE FIELD'S OUTER BORDER IS NOT AN ANCHOR: a border link does not exist (pd_has_* = 0), so pt_block can never call it a maximum. Fires once all neighbours' block flags are in (the same handshake pt_block itself uses — never an ordering assumption).

rules.name: pt_dist
rules.comment: THE DISTANCE FROM THE EDGE: pdist := 0 on an anchor, else 1 + the min over neighbours reachable across an UNBLOCKED link — THE SAME reachability pt_flood uses, so the distance is geodesic WITHIN the region and never crosses a boundary (Arend & Goldstein 1987: the code's domain of validity is its own compartment). Least fixed point from 0: monotone NON-DECREASING and bounded by the field's cell count, so it terminates. No threshold, no scale, no coordinate — a pure graph quantity.

rules.name: pt_decay
rules.comment: THE DECAY LENGTH, AND IT FALLS OUT (PROTOCOL §13). plam := the region's own MEAN GEODESIC DEPTH from its own boundary, Σpdist/n. It is GEOMETRY ONLY — no tuning, no threshold, no imported constant, no reference to any target output — and it is the SAME KIND OF OBJECT pt_fit1 already computes: pcen_r/pcen_c are the region's first moment in the row/column coordinate; plam is its first moment in the DISTANCE-TO-ITS-OWN-BOUNDARY coordinate. It is RELATIVE, not absolute: the code depends only on the dimensionless pdist/plam, so it rescales with the lattice. CLOSED FORM: a region anchored on ONE side has pdist uniform on 0..d_max, so plam = d_max/2 EXACTLY and the far-edge weight is plam/(plam+d_max) = 1/3, INDEPENDENT OF REGION WIDTH — the decay cuts the plane's far-field excursion to exactly one third. Nothing was chosen to make that 1/3. panch_n counts the region's anchors, so a region with NO boundary can be told apart from one whose boundary is everywhere. Geometry is counted over ALL the region's cells, sensed or not: depth does not need an observation.

rules.name: pt_paint
rules.comment: THE PAINT: every cell — sensed or not — takes ITS OWN hub's code at the hub's current korder. korder is read here and assigned NOWHERE but pt_escalate. The hub is found by pidx == this cell's pregion, which is unique by construction, so PickUnique is the honest read (PROTOCOL §12.3: `Pick` would silently return one of N). v1.1.0 — THE DECAY: the order-2 excursion is multiplied by w = plam/(plam+pdist), which is 1 AT the anchoring edge and STRICTLY DECREASING to 0 away from it, so the code is the fitted plane at the edge and relaxes to the order-1 constant far from it — never a constant-slope extrapolation across the far field, which is the operation Arend & Goldstein 1987 show is ill-posed and Cohen-Duwek & Spitzer 2019 show reconstructs the veridical image. DECLARED (PROTOCOL §13.1): the decay LENGTH falls out of the region's geometry, but the FALLOFF'S FORM is ARCHITECTURE — w is monotone BY CONSTRUCTION, so a decline-with-distance signature cannot fail to appear and is not evidence that one emerged.

rules.name: pt_resid
rules.comment: SUBTRACT. presid := |observed − painted| per channel, on OBSERVED cells only. A cell is REFUTED iff its residual reaches pquant/2 — the paint is then closer to a DIFFERENT representable value than to the observed one. pquant is the field's OWN integer alphabet step (in-frame is INTEGER; the paint is a cross-frame rendering and may be real). It is a RESOLUTION, not a tolerance: nothing is tuned, and a scale-invariance arm re-runs the whole battery at a ×4 alphabet.

rules.name: pt_escalate
rules.comment: K FALLS OUT OF THE RESIDUAL, and this is the ONLY rule that assigns korder. The region's order steps 1 -> 2 iff ANY of its observed cells is REFUTED at the order the residual was actually computed at (the presid_order handshake — never an ordering assumption). Nothing in the seed, the adapter or the tests chooses k: a flat surface stops at 1, a vague pattern reaches 2, and a surface the ladder cannot express reaches 2 and STAYS refuted. Monotone and capped by the built ladder, so it terminates.

rules.name: pt_verdict
rules.comment: THE MECHANISM SAYS WHETHER IT IS WRONG. At the top of the built ladder, prefuted := 1 iff some observed cell is STILL refuted — the ladder EXHAUSTED and the paint does not describe this surface. presid_mean is the readout (a measured magnitude, never a threshold).
